usage.callShape: POST https://ai.verifik.co/api/face-recognition/face-validation with JSON body {image} where image is a base64-encoded JPEG/PNG (data:image/jpeg;base64,... data-URI accepted)

inputExample.image: data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQSkZJRg...<base64 of a JPEG containing a human face>

usage.outputShape: body.data (Verifik face-detection result: bounding boxes + face quality signals) and body.signature — per the 402 bazaar output schema (untested; payment never completed)
quirks: 402 accepts entries are MALFORMED for x402 USDC: the Base USDC entry (eip155:8453, asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913) provides extra:{name:USDC,decimals:6} but OMITS the EIP-712 domain 'version' field. Sponge requires both name AND version to build the USDC transferWithAuthorization payload, so it aborts BEFORE sending any payment (error: 'EIP-712 domain parameters (name, version) are required'). No funds were spent across 2 attempts.

Endpoint defaults to Avalanche C-Chain (eip155:43114) for payment; also offers native AVAX/ETH and Base USDC. None of the accepts entries carry an EIP-712 'version', so all USDC paths are un-payable via Sponge as-is.

Alternative documented payment flow exists: pay on-chain manually then retry with header X-PAYMENT-TX=<txHash> (or Authorization: L402 <txHash>), or bypass with a Verifik user Bearer JWT — but neither is supported by the standard qa-pay/Sponge x402 flow.
Input schema is well-defined and simple: body {image} (base64). The endpoint itself is likely functional; only the payment-requirements 402 is broken for our stack.
usage.guide: Call POST https://ai.verifik.co/api/face-recognition/face-validation with JSON {"image": "<base64 JPEG of a human face>"} (a data:image/jpeg;base64,... URI works). Expect the face-detection result under body.data plus body.signature. WARNING: as of this test the endpoint cannot be paid via the standard x402 USDC flow — its 402 'accepts' entries omit the EIP-712 domain 'version' field, so the Sponge payment provider fails to build the payload and never sends funds. To use it you would need an alternate path (manual on-chain pay + X-PAYMENT-TX header, or a Verifik user Bearer JWT), neither of which qa-pay supports.
